gap: No result ChatGPT got gives the cost of making ChatGPT's $799 'budget option', the Snapmaker 2.0 A250T, eye-safe: the open-frame 2.0 is a Class 4 laser until you add Snapmaker's separately sold $269 Enclosure for Snapmaker 2.0, which Snapmaker lists with 'Laser Class 1 Safety … Door Detection'.
standout_why: I compared against desktop3dprinters.us/topics/3d-printer-laser-combos (cited in chat 1), desktop3dprinters.us/lists/3d-printers-with-laser-engraver (rank 1 in both chats, not cited), the desktop3dprinters software and 'what is a 3D laser printer' guides, 3dengr.com (cited in both chats) and engraverpicker.com's H2D review (rank 9, not cited). The lists page already says the bare laser module is Class 4 and the whole machine is Class 1 on every brand. It also says the open-frame Snapmaker 2.0 is Class 4 and that Snapmaker's separately sold enclosure brings it to Class 1, and that this enclosure pauses laser jobs when a door opens. The same page covers the H2S's 10 W-only limit and Bambu's 100 mm exhaust duct. engraverpicker already lists flame sensors and an emergency stop on the H2D laser edition. None of these pages gives the 2.0 enclosure's price, the Artisan's 36 CFM stock exhaust fan versus the 95 CFM upgrade Snapmaker pairs with the 20 W/40 W modules, or Snapmaker's goggle rating (OD6+ at 190–540 nm). 3dengr gives no laser class at all. The deciding mechanism is already on rank-1 pages, so this angle adds only the price and some detail.
decides: The mechanism is that every one of these lasers is Class 4 on its own. It only becomes Class 1 (eye-safe) inside a closed enclosure with door detection, plus Bambu's laser safety windows on the H2 series. That supports the H2D Laser Full Combo and the Artisan as the real picks, because each comes as a closed Class 1 machine. It counts against ChatGPT's $799 Snapmaker 2.0 A250T card: that machine is open-frame Class 4, so it needs the $269 enclosure (about $1,068 total) or OD6+ goggles. That total is close to the $1,799 Artisan Standard on Snapmaker's US store today. It also shows ChatGPT's $2,599 RobotShop Artisan price is $800 above the maker's price.

findings.label: Enclosure for Snapmaker 2.0: price and what it does for laser safety
findings.value: $269 (compare-at $599); 'Laser Class 1 Safety: Enclosure Panels Specially Designed for Laser Reduction; Door Detection'; built-in exhaust system

findings.note: Read from the store's product data with storecheck.py. With the enclosure, ChatGPT's $799 A250T card comes to $799 + $269 = $1,068 for a Class 1 setup.

findings.label: Laser class and the eye protection Snapmaker requires
findings.value: Class 4. Snapmaker says 'always use these lasers with an Enclosure or Laser Safety Goggles (190-540nm OD6+ and 900-1700nm OD4+)'. 40 W module with air assist: $429.
findings.source_title: Snapmaker 40W Laser Module with Air Assist – Snapmaker US store
findings.note: storecheck.py search. The same page says 'The Artisan Enclosure is not available for online purchase' (you have to contact info@snapmaker.com). Listed as compatible with the 2.0 A350T/A350/A250T/A250/F350/F250, the Artisan and the Ray. The A150 takes the 20 W only.

findings.label: Laser fume exhaust: stock fan vs upgrade
findings.value: The enclosure's stock exhaust fan is rated 36 CFM, which Snapmaker says is 'sufficient for the use of the 10W Laser Module'. The Boosted Exhaust Fan is 95 CFM ($17.99) and Snapmaker says it is 'particularly beneficial when using the 20W/40W Laser Module'.
findings.source_title: Boosted Exhaust Fan for Snapmaker Artisan – Snapmaker US store
findings.note: storecheck.py search. CFM figures are Snapmaker's maximum airflow ratings.
